ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Definition: If a moving point P satisfies the condition that the distances from P to the two endpoints of a line segment $AB$ are in the ratio $PA = 4PB$, then P is called the $KZ$ point of the line segment $AB$. However, point P is not considered a $KZ$ point of the line segment $BA$. As illustrated in the diagram, within a rhombus $ABCD$ where $AB=8$ and $\angle B=120^\circ$, points E and F are located on $BC$ and $CD$ respectively, satisfying $\angle AEF=120^\circ$. By connecting $AF$, assuming point E is the $KZ$ point of line segment $AF$, what is the length of $DF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 3, take $CJ$ on $CB$ such that $CJ=CF$.\\
Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus,\\
it follows that $AB=BC=CD=AD=8$, $AB\parallel CD$,\\
hence $\angle B+\angle C=180^\circ$,\\
since $\angle B=120^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle C=60^\circ$,\\
since $CJ=CF$,\\
it follows that $\triangle CFJ$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
thus $FJ=CF=CJ$, $\angle CJF=60^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle FJE=120^\circ=\angle B$,\\
since point E is the $KZ$ point on the line segment $AF$,\\
it follows that $AE=4EF$,\\
since $\angle AEC=\angle AEF+\angle FEJ=\angle B+\angle BAE$, $\angle AEF=\angle B=120^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle FEJ=\angle BAE$,\\
therefore $\triangle ABE\sim \triangle EJF$,\\
thus $\frac{AB}{EJ}=\frac{BE}{FJ}=\frac{AE}{EF}=4$,\\
thus $EJ=2$, $BE=4FJ=4CJ$,\\
thus $BC=BE+EJ+CJ=4CJ+2+CJ=8$,\\
i.e., $CJ=\frac{6}{5}$,\\
therefore $CF=CJ=\frac{6}{5}$,\\
thus $DF=CD-CF=8-\frac{6}{5}=\boxed{\frac{34}{5}}$.

By the definition of KZ point, E is the KZ point of segment AF, and the endpoint order is AF, so EA=4EF. Also because E is on BC, C, J, E are collinear, and ∠AEC can be divided into ∠AEF+∠FEJ; it is known that ∠AEF=120°=∠B. At the same time, in triangle ABE, EC is the extension direction of EB, so the exterior angle ∠AEC=∠B+∠BAE. Comparing gives ∠FEJ=∠BAE. Thus triangle ABE and triangle EJF have two corresponding angles equal: ∠B=∠FJE, ∠BAE=∠FEJ, therefore triangle ABE∼triangle EJF. 先描述图像：图中右侧的图3显示一个菱形ABCD，A在左侧，B在左下，C在右侧，D在上方；E位于边BC上，F位于边CD上，并且画出了AE、AF、EF。图中没有标出辅助点J，因此按方法在边CB上取一点J，使CJ=CF。

再推理：菱形ABCD中，AB=BC=CD=AD=8，且AB∥CD。已知∠B=120°，所以相邻内角∠C=180°-120°=60°。因为J在CB上、F在CD上，且CJ=CF，而∠JCF=∠C=60°，所以三角形CFJ为等边三角形。因此FJ=CJ=CF，且∠CJF=60°。由于J、E、B、C共线，射线JE与JC方向相反，所以∠FJE=180°-60°=120°，等于∠B。

由KZ点定义，E是线段AF的KZ点，且端点顺序为AF，所以EA=4EF。又因为E在BC上，C、J、E共线，∠AEC可以分成∠AEF+∠FEJ；已知∠AEF=120°=∠B。同时在三角形ABE中，EC是EB的延长方向，所以外角∠AEC=∠B+∠BAE。比较可得∠FEJ=∠BAE。于是三角形ABE与三角形EJF有两角对应相等：∠B=∠FJE，∠BAE=∠FEJ，因此三角形ABE∼三角形EJF。

raw_record.original_question: Definition: If a moving point P satisfies the condition that the distances from P to the two endpoints of a line segment $AB$ are in the ratio $PA = 4PB$, then P is called the $KZ$ point of the line segment $AB$. However, point P is not considered a $KZ$ point of the line segment $BA$. As illustrated in the diagram, within a rhombus $ABCD$ where $AB=8$ and $\angle B=120^\circ$, points E and F are located on $BC$ and $CD$ respectively, satisfying $\angle AEF=120^\circ$. By connecting $AF$, assuming point E is the $KZ$ point of line segment $AF$, what is the length of $DF$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 3, take $CJ$ on $CB$ such that $CJ=CF$.\\
Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus,\\
it follows that $AB=BC=CD=AD=8$, $AB\parallel CD$,\\
hence $\angle B+\angle C=180^\circ$,\\
since $\angle B=120^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle C=60^\circ$,\\
since $CJ=CF$,\\
it follows that $\triangle CFJ$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
thus $FJ=CF=CJ$, $\angle CJF=60^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle FJE=120^\circ=\angle B$,\\
since point E is the $KZ$ point on the line segment $AF$,\\
it follows that $AE=4EF$,\\
since $\angle AEC=\angle AEF+\angle FEJ=\angle B+\angle BAE$, $\angle AEF=\angle B=120^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle FEJ=\angle BAE$,\\
therefore $\triangle ABE\sim \triangle EJF$,\\
thus $\frac{AB}{EJ}=\frac{BE}{FJ}=\frac{AE}{EF}=4$,\\
thus $EJ=2$, $BE=4FJ=4CJ$,\\
thus $BC=BE+EJ+CJ=4CJ+2+CJ=8$,\\
i.e., $CJ=\frac{6}{5}$,\\
therefore $CF=CJ=\frac{6}{5}$,\\
thus $DF=CD-CF=8-\frac{6}{5}=\boxed{\frac{34}{5}}$

The auxiliary point J is not marked in the diagram, so according to the method, take a point J on side CB such that CJ=CF.

Then reason: In rhombus ABCD, AB=BC=CD=AD=8, and AB∥CD. It is known that ∠B=120°, so the adjacent interior angle ∠C=180°-120°=60°. Because J is on CB, F is on CD, and CJ=CF, while ∠JCF=∠C=60°, triangle CFJ is an equilateral triangle. Therefore FJ=CJ=CF, and ∠CJF=60°. By the definition of KZ point, E is the KZ point of segment AF, and the endpoint order is AF, so EA=4EF. Also because E is on BC, C, J, E are collinear, and ∠AEC can be divided into ∠AEF+∠FEJ; it is known that ∠AEF=120°=∠B. At the same time, in triangle ABE, EC is the extension direction of EB, so the exterior angle ∠AEC=∠B+∠BAE. Comparing gives ∠FEJ=∠BAE. Thus triangle ABE and triangle EJF have two corresponding angles equal: ∠B=∠FJE, ∠BAE=∠FEJ, therefore triangle ABE∼triangle EJF.

The similarity ratio is obtained from AE:EF=4:1, so AB:EJ=BE:FJ=AE:EF=4:1. Because AB=8, EJ=8/4=2; and FJ=CJ, so BE=4FJ=4CJ. Along the direction of BC, BC=BE+EJ+CJ=4CJ+2+CJ=8, therefore 5CJ=6, CJ=6/5. Thus CF=CJ=6/5. Finally DF=CD-CF=8-6/5=34/5.
